title: 六级篇章听力：轮班安排与地图收藏
instruction: 听完整一节2篇短文及各段后读出的问题，依次选择最佳答案。音频中材料和问题各读一遍，卷面只印四个选项。本原创使用节内编号1—7，各段对应1—3、4—7题。播放器可回听，正式单次听辨条件未强制。
audio_introduction: Section B. You will hear two passages. After each, you will hear questions. Each recording and each question will be spoken only once. Choose the best answer from A, B, C and D.
source_form_notice: 六级形式参照2024年12月第一套转载Section B：2段、3/4共7回应、每题四选；原创采用节内编号，问题只在录音与作者区。全部自有虚构内容及本机合成试听，非原考试原声；未独立教研/听辨/学生难度或产品等值验证。

turns.speaker: R
turns.text: The following fictional account concerns a small translation office trying a more flexible working day. Its manager initially offered everybody the same freedom to choose a starting time. She expected the arrangement to be simple because each translator could work independently for much of the day. Within a week, however, urgent queries were accumulating late in the afternoon, when several experienced staff had already left. The difficulty was not that those people were working fewer hours. Their hours no longer overlapped with the period when their advice was most often needed. The manager could have required everyone to return to the old schedule. Instead, she asked the team to identify tasks that genuinely needed simultaneous availability and tasks that did not. They agreed on a shorter shared period, with separate arrangements for an urgent query outside it. Flexibility remained possible for most individual work. The revised arrangement was less identical for every role, but the reasons for the differences were written down and reviewed with the staff affected. After a month, fewer queries waited until the next day. The office did not announce that flexible hours had increased translation quality; it had measured waiting, not the accuracy of the finished work. The manager says the useful lesson was about coordination. Giving everyone the same choice had looked fair on paper, but it had hidden unequal dependencies between tasks. A workable agreement had to recognise those dependencies without assuming that every hour of every person's work needed to occur at the same time.

questions.spoken_question: What caused urgent queries to accumulate?
options: A
Translators had stopped completing their contracted hours.
B
Staff availability no longer matched the time advice was needed.
C
The office had dismissed all experienced employees.
D
Every query required the entire team to be present.
questions.rationale: B总时未少但重叠错时，A明确非少时，C未裁，D只部分需同步。

questions.spoken_question: How did the office revise its arrangement?
options: A
It abolished all freedom over starting times.
B
It made every task depend on the same eight-hour meeting.
C
It stopped accepting queries from customers.
D
It identified shared availability needs while retaining flexibility elsewhere.
questions.rationale: D短共享段加urgent规则其余灵活；A/B/C反或未述。

questions.spoken_question: What limitation did the office retain when reporting the result?
options: A
Reduced waiting did not establish better translation accuracy.
B
No queries had been recorded before the change.
C
The trial proved every role should have identical hours.
D
The office could no longer compare any schedules.
questions.rationale: A测waiting非accuracy；B无未记声明，C反，D仍能review。

turns.speaker: R
turns.text: For the fictional map collector Martin Vale, a map's most interesting feature is not always the accuracy of its roads. He began by collecting maps used by his own family. One had a pencil circle around a campsite that was never reached. Another carried a shopping list on the back. These marks could seem to damage the printed object, but Martin saw them as evidence of how a map entered somebody's life. When a local gallery proposed an exhibition, its first plan was to display only the cleanest maps, arranged by publication date. Martin suggested adding the marked copies and a short explanation of what was known about their use. He did not claim that every pencil mark could be interpreted. Some were anonymous, and a crossed-out route did not reveal whether a journey had been cancelled or merely changed. The exhibition kept those uncertainties visible. Visitors could compare the formal route printed on the page with the personal record added afterwards. To avoid overwhelming the display, the gallery chose a few well-documented examples rather than filling every wall. A separate catalogue listed the remaining maps without pretending they had all been equally researched. Martin was pleased when one visitor said she had never thought about the unused side of a map before. For him, collecting had become less about rescuing perfect objects and more about keeping the traces of imperfect use understandable. He still cared whether a road was correctly drawn. He simply refused to treat that as the only question a map could invite.

questions.spoken_question: What first interested Martin about the family maps?
options: A
They had all been printed in the same year.
B
They showed roads absent from every official map.
C
Personal marks revealed something about their use.
D
Their owners had kept them completely untouched.
questions.rationale: C笔圈/购物单体现生活使用；A/B无全同年/独有路，D有痕非无触。

questions.spoken_question: How did Martin respond to the gallery’s first plan?
options: A
He suggested including marked copies with explanations of their use.
B
He insisted that all publication dates be hidden.
C
He demanded that every map fill a separate wall.
D
He asked the gallery to remove all clean maps.
questions.rationale: A加marked与所知use；B未隐日期，C选择少量非每墙，D不是去尽clean。

questions.spoken_question: Why were some uncertainties mentioned in the exhibition?
options: A
The gallery wanted visitors to invent the missing facts.
B
Every pencilled route proved a journey had been completed.
C
Martin had refused to examine any marks.
D
Marks did not always reveal who made them or what had happened.
questions.rationale: D匿名/划路线不能证取消或改；A不造事实，B反未达camp，C有查非拒。

questions.spoken_question: What was the purpose of the separate catalogue?
options: A
To certify that every remaining map had been equally researched.
B
To list further maps without overstating how fully they were understood.
C
To replace all the displayed examples with shopping lists.
D
To prove that road accuracy was never worth considering.
questions.rationale: B列其余但不假同研究充分，A反，C无，D末仍重roadaccuracy。
